q: Some tiny dung beetles hitchhike in mammal fur. What resource are they waiting to obtain?
d: Riding on sloths or monkeys puts them close to the source of their next meal.
evidence: Curator describes beetles clinging to sloth or monkey fur awaiting fresh dung.

q: Despite being called a dung beetle, the Peruvian Deltochilum valgum hunts which living prey?
d: Some members of this familiar scavenging group have evolved a predatory diet.
evidence: Museum account identifies millipede predation by this species.

q: Why does a mother earwig repeatedly lick her eggs?
d: She guards the clutch, gathers scattered eggs and cleans their surfaces.
choices: To mark each egg with a scent
To feed embryos through the shell
To dissolve the shells before hatching
evidence: Museum reproductive account describes licking off fungi and parasites.

q: How do an earwig’s large hindwings fit beneath its tiny protective wing covers?
d: The thin semicircular wings fold into a compact package beneath the small covers.
choices: Stretching and shrinking an elastic membrane
evidence: Museum describes large membranous semicircular hindwings folding beneath tegmina.

q: A tsetse fly nourishes her developing larva inside her body with what?
d: One larva develops at a time and receives nutrients from a specialized maternal gland.
choices: Fragments of her own gut lining
evidence: First-party laboratory account describes intrauterine larva and milk gland.

q: What can turn an otherwise edible berry meal into an intoxicating one for cedar waxwings?
d: Alcohol can accumulate in overripe fruit eaten by these fruit-loving birds.
evidence: Zoo explicitly reports intoxication from fermented berries.

q: During courtship, cedar waxwing pairs may repeatedly do what with a berry or flower petal?
d: The small exchanged object is part of the pair’s display.
choices: Balance it on the nest rim
Drop it while flying in formation
evidence: Zoo describes paired birds exchanging small objects during courtship.

q: In windless laboratory conditions, what helped tiny spiders lift off on strands of silk?
d: Fields comparable to atmospheric ones triggered ballooning and supplied lift.
s: University of Bristol · Spiders go ballooning
evidence: First-party experiment switched electric fields on/off and changed spider altitude.

q: When Betty the New Caledonian crow needed a hook to lift a food bucket, what did she do?
a: Bent a straight piece of wire
d: She reshaped an unfamiliar material into a working tool and repeated the feat.
choices: Twisted a leaf into a rope
Bent a straight piece of wire
s: University of Oxford · Crow tool manufacture
evidence: Researchers document Betty wedging and bending wire into usable hooks.

q: A scrub-jay that was watched hiding food may later protect the stash by doing what?
a: Moving it to another hiding place
d: Experiments show that the birds track which individual saw particular caches and adjust their relocation behavior.
choices: Storing it in a shared pile
Posting another jay as a guard
Moving it to another hiding place
evidence: Primary abstract reports observer-specific recaching; does not assert humanlike mind-reading.

q: An ogre-faced spider can catch prey flying behind it by detecting airborne sound with which body parts?
d: Sensitive structures let sound trigger a rapid backward net-casting strike.
evidence: Researchers confirm leg metatarsal sensitivity and airborne-prey strikes.

q: Bottlenose dolphins can address a particular companion by copying what individually distinctive sound?
d: Playback experiments found dolphins responding to synthetic versions of their own whistle pattern.
s: University of St Andrews · Dolphin names
evidence: First-party report describes signature-whistle copying and individual playback responses.

q: Sleeping sperm whales can float beneath the surface in what unusual posture?
d: Groups may rest upright in the water rather than swimming continuously or lying on the bottom.
choices: With the tail permanently above water
Flat on their backs at the seabed
s: University of St Andrews · Sperm whale rest
evidence: Researchers document vertical rest beneath the surface and buoyancy regulation.

q: Night recordings at three European zoos revealed giraffes making which unexpected sound?
d: Researchers recorded sustained low-frequency vocalizations; their precise social function remained unresolved.
s: BMC Research Notes · Baotic et al., 2015
evidence: Primary indexed study reports nocturnal humming, without established behavioral function.

q: What signal from inside a Nile crocodile nest can prompt the mother to begin digging it open?
d: Embryos call before emerging, providing information to both their mother and their siblings.
choices: Burst of scent from broken yolks
The sound of shells scraping together
evidence: Primary abstract identifies prehatching calls targeting mothers and siblings.

q: Young Boulengerula taitana caecilians use special teeth to peel and eat what their mother provides?
d: The mother develops a nutrient-rich skin layer that the young strip off during parental care.
evidence: Primary paper directly describes young peeling and eating modified maternal skin.

q: A single empty shell can trigger a chain of house moves among hermit crabs. How does the chain work?
a: Each takes the shell vacated by a larger crab
d: Crabs can wait in a size-ordered group until an animal fits the newly available shell.
choices: All share the new shell temporarily
Each takes the shell vacated by a larger crab
The largest breaks the shell into pieces
Each steals from the smallest crab
s: National Park Service · Hermit crab vacancy chains
evidence: Institutional account describes waiting crabs and a cascading exchange of shells.

q: Nesting chinstrap penguins were found to accumulate sleep through what remarkable strategy?
d: Brain recordings showed extremely brief sleep bouts adding up to substantial daily sleep.
evidence: Primary abstract reports over10,000 daily bouts averaging about4seconds.

q: How do bearded vultures give naturally pale breast feathers their rusty orange color?
d: The coloring is acquired from mineral-rich pools rather than grown as orange feather pigment.
choices: Applying oily secretions from their beaks
evidence: Conservation breeding organization describes iron-oxide bathing and white captive birds without suitable pools.

q: Why do New World vultures let liquid waste run down their legs on hot days?
d: The wet bare skin loses heat as the liquid evaporates.
choices: To make their toes grip better
s: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance · Vulture wonders
evidence: Zoo account describes urohydrosis cooling by evaporation.

q: A threatened vulture may do what immediately before escaping?
d: Losing the load can aid flight; the abandoned food may also distract a pursuer.
s: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance · Vulture wonders
evidence: Zoo account describes regurgitation reducing load and delaying predators.

q: How does a loggerhead shrike secure prey in its outdoor larder?
a: Impales it on thorns or barbed wire
d: The songbird pins victims in place for eating immediately or storing for later.
choices: Stores it in a nest cavity
Impales it on thorns or barbed wire
s: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service · Shrike larders
evidence: Agency observations document impaled prey on thorny trees and wire.

q: The fine cracks in African elephant skin help the animal keep cool by retaining what?
d: Liquid held in the channels prolongs evaporative cooling after wetting.
s: University of Geneva · Elephant skin cracks
evidence: Institutional research account links cracking to water retention and cooling.

q: Although horses can doze standing up, what must they normally do for sustained REM sleep?
d: Muscle tone drops during REM sleep, so standing cannot support that stage reliably.
choices: Rest the head on a support
evidence: Laboratory account distinguishes standing slow-wave sleep from recumbent REM sleep.

q: What makes up most of a palm-nut vulture’s unusually unvulturelike diet?
d: Much of its diet comes from plants, although it also eats small animals.
s: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance · Vulture wonders
evidence: Zoo account reports mainly palm nuts, fruits and grain plus small animals.
